scope.program: Troubled Asset Relief Program Capital Purchase Program
scope.primary_transaction: Marshall & Ilsley Corporation CPP investment and Bank of Montreal repayment transaction
scope.question: Did the public receive contractually structured and realized value recovery from capital, authority and risk supplied to private banks, and what does that result not recover?

sources.title: Treasury Announces TARP Capital Purchase Program Description
supports: Treasury purchase of senior preferred shares as Tier 1 capital rather than a grant
five-percent annual dividends for the first five years and nine percent thereafter
warrants to purchase common stock with an aggregate market price equal to fifteen percent of the senior preferred investment for publicly traded institutions
executive-compensation and corporate-governance conditions, including a clawback for materially inaccurate earnings-based incentive compensation
does_not_support: the later realized return
that every participating institution received identical economic terms
public voting control over ordinary bank operations
full recovery of systemic, household or distributional costs

sources.title: Capital Purchase Program Overview
supports: capital supplied to 707 financial institutions in 48 states
Treasury receipt of preferred stock or debt securities rather than grant treatment
five-percent and nine-percent dividend structure for most participants
warrants or other securities designed to let taxpayers receive additional returns as banks recovered
does_not_support: the complete recipient-selection denominator or every rejected applicant
equal benefit to every taxpayer, borrower, worker or homeowner
that taxpayer upside was proportionate to all public risk and externalities
public co-governance over participating banks

sources.title: Treasury Announces Warrant Repurchase and Disposition Process for the Capital Purchase Program
supports: issuer repurchase at fair market value through a contractually defined process
independent-appraiser procedure when Treasury and an issuer could not agree
Treasury use of market, model and third-party inputs to protect taxpayer value
authority to liquidate warrants when the issuer did not repurchase them
does_not_support: that every valuation maximized public return
absence of political, market-timing or information asymmetry
individual taxpayer participation in valuation decisions
the final program-wide return

sources.title: Treasury Releases TARP Warrant Disposition Report
supports: the stated purpose of warrants was additional potential taxpayer return
four billion dollars in gross warrant-disposition proceeds from 34 banks as of December 31, 2009
reported additional absolute return from warrants beyond dividends for that bounded cohort
does_not_support: the eventual return on the entire CPP portfolio
risk-adjusted proportionality
that warrant proceeds reached directly affected households
complete public governance rights

candidate.title: TARP Capital Purchase Program public capital, warrants and realized value recovery
candidate.question: Did the public retain and realize a share of value created or preserved through public capital, authority and crisis risk supplied to private banks, and which broader costs and affected populations remained outside that recovery?

primary_transaction.repayment_path: Bank of Montreal acquired the institution and purchased the outstanding CPP preferred shares
primary_transaction.additional_public_proceeds: $214.6 million in earlier dividends, $11.9 million in final accrued dividends and $3.3 million for the warrant

program_result.gross_recovered: $226.8 billion through repayments, dividends, interest and other income

recovery_chain.observation: Treasury used TARP authority and public financing capacity to provide capital during a financial crisis, accepting substantial financial risk.
recovery_chain.limit: The sources do not monetize the complete systemic, distributional, political or opportunity costs of the intervention.

recovery_chain.observation: Treasury received senior preferred stock or debt, dividends, warrants, transfer and disposition rights, and bounded governance and compensation conditions rather than issuing grants.
recovery_chain.limit: The preferred shares were generally nonvoting outside bounded class rights and did not create public co-governance over ordinary bank strategy.

recovery_chain.observation: Warrants were expressly intended to let taxpayers receive additional returns as recipient banks recovered, beyond repayment and dividends.
recovery_chain.limit: Potential upside did not establish that taxpayers captured all recovery value or were compensated for every public risk.

recovery_chain.observation: Repurchase and disposal used contractually defined fair-market-value procedures, Treasury valuation, independent appraisers when necessary and third-party sales when issuers did not repurchase.
recovery_chain.limit: The public record does not prove that every timing and valuation decision maximized return.

recovery_chain.observation: The M&I transaction joined original public capital to preferred-share repayment, dividends, warrant proceeds and a stated $229.8 million positive return.
recovery_chain.limit: One positive transaction does not establish the result for every participant or the social counterfactual without intervention.

recovery_chain.observation: CPP closed after recovering more gross proceeds than invested and Treasury's final table reports $16.307 billion in CPP net income after write-offs, losses and Treasury interest expense.
recovery_chain.limit: CPP income cannot be generalized to TARP as a whole, which had an estimated $31.1 billion net cost.

recovery_chain.observation: Value was recovered to the federal public account on behalf of taxpayers.
recovery_chain.limit: The mechanism did not itself establish direct compensation, governance or proportional recovery for foreclosed homeowners, displaced workers, borrowers or communities bearing crisis harms.

recovery_chain.observation: Preferred returns and warrants created measurable public upside linked to the public capital contribution.
recovery_chain.limit: The record does not establish that the recovered amount was proportionate to total public risk, liquidity support, market backstop, crisis externalities or opportunity cost.

recovery_chain.observation: All CPP assets were ultimately repaid, sold, written off or otherwise resolved, and the program closed with no remaining OFS troubled assets.
recovery_chain.limit: Program closure does not answer long-run concentration, moral hazard or distributional effects in the banking system.

recovery_chain.observation: The structure demonstrates one mechanism by which public capital can carry preferred returns, warrants, clawbacks, valuation rules and exit rights.
recovery_chain.limit: Transfer to AI, defense, infrastructure, data or platform financing requires sector-specific legal, valuation, governance, performance and failure records.

propositions.claim: The public supplied capital, authority and substantial financial risk to private financial institutions through the CPP.
counterevidence: CPP targeted viable institutions rather than treating every recipient as insolvent
the intervention sought financial stability and was not designed primarily as an investment fund
the total public-risk denominator extends beyond Treasury disbursements
propositions.falsifier: The funds were ordinary private capital without public fiscal exposure, authority or downside risk.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep fiscal contribution, systemic backstop and broader crisis cost as separate ledgers.

propositions.claim: CPP embedded ex ante public recovery rights through preferred stock or debt, dividends, warrants and bounded contractual protections.
counterevidence: preferred shares were generally nonvoting outside limited class rights
terms varied by institution type and later program changes
contractual protections did not eliminate losses
propositions.falsifier: Treasury received only unsecured repayment promises with no dividend, warrant, transfer, valuation or protective rights.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not convert financial rights into full public governance.

propositions.claim: CPP warrants were deliberately designed to give taxpayers residual upside as recipient banks recovered.
counterevidence: warrant quantity and form varied
some warrants were reduced following qualifying equity offerings
realized value depended on valuation and market timing
propositions.falsifier: Program records show warrants were unrelated to taxpayer recovery or produced no additional public proceeds.
propositions.stopping_rule: Distinguish intended upside, realized proceeds and proportional recovery.

propositions.claim: The M&I transaction closes one exact contribution-to-rights-to-realized-return chain.
counterevidence: the calculation is nominal rather than a complete risk-adjusted social return
the result depended on a bank acquisition and did not represent every CPP exit
the record does not allocate the return to specific affected people
propositions.falsifier: The listed dividends, warrant proceeds or repayment were not received, were double counted or were less than the original public investment after the bounded transaction costs.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not generalize from M&I without the program-wide denominator.

propositions.claim: The CPP as a whole produced realized net income for the public after program losses and Treasury interest expense.
counterevidence: gross recovery and net income are different measures
CBO and Treasury report a net cost for TARP as a whole
the accounting does not capture every social and macroeconomic cost
propositions.falsifier: Final audited or official records show CPP net cost rather than net income after losses and financing expense.
propositions.stopping_rule: Keep the R7 assignment bounded to CPP financial recovery.

propositions.claim: CPP's positive return proves that TARP as a whole was profitable and fully repaid every public cost.
counterevidence: TARP contained programs with different purposes and recovery expectations
bank-investment programs collectively produced positive returns
financial stabilization may have generated benefits not captured in program cash flows
propositions.falsifier: A complete official accounting shows no TARP net cost and closes all material fiscal, social and opportunity costs.
propositions.stopping_rule: Never use one profitable subprogram as the total-program denominator.

propositions.claim: Aggregate taxpayer recovery under CPP directly compensated the households, workers, borrowers and communities that bore crisis harms.
counterevidence: public-account recovery can still benefit the general fiscal position
separate housing and relief programs addressed other populations
the intervention may have reduced broader economic harm
propositions.falsifier: A CPP-specific distribution record joins the affected population's contribution or injury to direct compensation, ownership, governance or a proportionate share of recovered value.
propositions.stopping_rule: Public institutional recovery and direct affected-person recovery remain different R7 forms.

propositions.claim: Preferred stock and warrants gave taxpayers full co-governance over participating banks.
counterevidence: executive-compensation conditions and class rights imposed real constraints
Treasury had disposition, valuation and repayment authority
some program documents provided board-observer or appointment routes in specified circumstances
propositions.falsifier: The operative agreements gave affected publics or accountable representatives enforceable authority over ordinary bank purpose, strategy, thresholds, use and termination comparable to R6 co-governance.
propositions.stopping_rule: Do not infer R6 from R7 financial rights.

propositions.claim: The final CPP return was proportionate to the full public risk, market backstop, opportunity cost and crisis externalities.
counterevidence: the final financial return exceeded the program's direct accounting cost
the intervention's purpose was stabilization rather than profit maximization
counterfactual losses without intervention are difficult to identify
propositions.falsifier: A comprehensive risk-adjusted and distributional accounting shows material public under-recovery or full proportional recovery against a defined denominator.
propositions.stopping_rule: Name the risk denominator before making a proportionality claim.

propositions.claim: The CPP recovery architecture can be transferred directly to public financing of AI, defense, data, infrastructure or platform companies.
counterevidence: preferred returns, warrants, clawbacks and exit rights are legally portable concepts
public venture, subsidy and procurement programs already use some analogous rights
bank capital regulation and crisis conditions were institutionally specific
propositions.falsifier: Matched sector-specific programs show that the rights are legally unavailable, operationally ineffective, value-destructive or displaced by equivalent private control.
propositions.stopping_rule: Require one exact receiving program with contribution, rights, performance, recovery, failure and affected-public records.

propositions.claim: This single U.S. banking case satisfies the complete M-05 works standard.
counterevidence: the case supplies an observed R7 mechanism to the answer library
the R6 works-council control supplies a separate higher-order governance mechanism
other M-05 cases cover R2 through R5
propositions.falsifier: A combined architecture demonstrates the required answer dimensions across at least three domains and two jurisdictions with durability and no equivalent displacement.
propositions.stopping_rule: A library of distributed controls is not yet one repeatable complete answer.

current_result.strongest_result: CPP joined public capital and crisis risk to preferred returns, warrants, fair-value disposition and a final $16.307 billion program net income; the M&I transaction supplies an exact $229.8 million positive-return chain.
current_result.largest_limit: The recovery belongs to the public fiscal account, not directly to every person harmed by the crisis, and proportionality to total public risk and social cost remains unresolved.
